A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LIAR framework. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, experiments and visual results can be matched despite appendix reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original occupancy experiments on Occ3D-nuScenes and nuScenes-C, component ablations, enhancement comparisons and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds learned-enhancement comparisons, daytime evaluation and additional computational measurements.

M1.justification: The SLLIE, 2D-IGS and 3D-IDP procedures, architecture and occupancy losses remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 newly documents the existing SCI pretraining objective; both versions already specify nighttime pretraining and frozen enhancement weights.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on clean daytime scenes and the full Occ3D-nuScenes evaluation set in Appendix A.5/Table 7. Daytime data already appeared in v1 training, but its evaluations targeted real and synthetic nighttime conditions. No new dataset is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds LCDPNet and CSEC preprocessing combined with each of BEVDetOcc, FlashOcc and COTR, substantially expanding the relevant enhancement comparators beyond v1's classical methods. OPUS joins the computational comparison, and COTR replaces FlashOcc in the appendix visual comparisons. Main Tables 1–2 retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: v3 introduces enhancement-preprocessing controls and parameter-count/FPS evaluation metrics. Its computational table uses the existing mixed day/night-training accuracy results instead of the night-only-training results used in v1. The retained benchmark splits, optimizer and 24-epoch schedule are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new paired enhancement controls in Table 6 test whether preprocessing alone explains LIAR's advantage across three occupancy backbones. They supplement the retained classical-enhancement comparisons. The original component, threshold, sampling and illumination-field ablations in Table 3 and Figure 8 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the performance comparisons. The existing illumination and sampling-offset distribution analyses are retained, without a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results, but substantial supplementary results are added. Table 6 reports COTR+LCDPNet at 20.22 and COTR+CSEC at 20.17 versus LIAR at 22.09 mIoU. Table 7 adds LIAR's 40.42 daytime and 39.57 overall mIoU; Table 4 adds speed and parameter results. Appendix A.5 reverses the daytime/overall gains over COTR: the table implies 0.95 and 0.87, respectively.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds an explicit mathematical definition of the stage-wise SCI fidelity loss in Equation 16, including its illumination and calibration variables. This formalizes previously undocumented pretraining mathematics. Equations 1–15 and the threshold-selection reasoning remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same nighttime occupancy framework, three proposed components and claim of up to a 7.9-point advantage. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking joint-training collapse to overbright SCI pseudo-targets, interpreting the enhancement controls as evidence for illumination-aware processing, and extending applicability to daytime scenes. Its limitations discuss synthetic-to-real differences in scene semantics and sensor degradation, while removing v1's explicit warning about inaccurate illumination estimation under irregular lighting.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 specifies the SCI fidelity objective and clarifies that SLLIE pretraining uses the nighttime training split. These are additional details of the existing procedure. The main optimizer, learning rate, loss weights, hardware and code/pretrained-model access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion now explicitly contrasts selective enhancement with LCDPNet and CSEC. Citations broaden to additional detection, depth-completion, super-resolution and occupancy work, while references including DFA3D and DualBEV are removed. The central positioning around illumination-aware nighttime occupancy remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 revises selected introduction and related-work passages, rewrites the limitations, reorganizes and expands the appendix, and adds author notes and acknowledgments. Most method explanations, experimental discussion and contribution wording are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 6–7 and expands the computational table with an OPUS row and parameter/FPS columns. Appendix tables and final figures are reordered, visual comparison panels substitute COTR for FlashOcc, and Figure 4 gains a pixel label. The main figures, benchmark-table structures and overall design are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's classical-enhancement tests, v3 supplies more relevant learned-enhancement controls for LIAR's claimed benefit. Daytime results, speed measurements and pretraining details also improve assessment of applicability and computational cost. These provide a useful, limited strengthening of the paper, tempered by Appendix A.5's reversed performance margins and removal of the illumination-estimation limitation.
